lines: A bustling street outside the law. With no rules or order, only violence and desire ruled this city, and we stood in the middle of a battlefield like hell.
Revy
Fuck!! Did we just wander into a Class B panic horror?!
Revy shot the Ghouls down one by one as they swarmed in, spreading a stench of rot.
She bounced, shot, and felled them as if dancing. Her movements were light, yet ferocious.
Revy
Tch, these undead bastards. They're way too tough to deal with!
In that instant, the air grew gritty. A faint mist rose and swayed.
Me
"...Here they come. Vampires..."!
Red eyes emerged from the mist. Feeling a resolve that would never let us escape, it charged at us, leading the Ghouls.
Revy readied her stance, a smile on her face.
Revy
Hah... you bunch of ghosts. Perfect. I'll send you all back to hell in one go!
Time rewound to six hours earlier.
Based on a connection from a past mission, I had been asked by Revy for "a little help with a job."
The details were simple. Infiltrate a Western-style mansion on the outskirts and retrieve a jewelry box for a certain collector. That was all.
It had apparently once been the residence of a powerful figure, but now it seemed to be an abandoned house with no one living there.
The infiltration itself was easy. Revy's boldness and my caution meshed perfectly, allowing us to easily break in through the attic of the old mansion.
The air inside was stiflingly humid, giving off an atmosphere like a haunted house.
Revy
Damn it... but is there really a jewelry box or something?
Me
According to the intel, it should be stored around here.
Revy
I guess I have no choice but to believe it. The pay isn't bad, anyway. Wait, is that it?
The target item—a metal decorative box—sat alone on a shelf. Revy took it with a sly grin.
Revy
Big deal. This is a piece of cake.
But then, in that very moment...
The air changed. A chill that pierced the skin, tinnitus, and the presence of something crawling up from behind.
Revy
...What the hell was that?
Me
...I felt a barrier-like presence react. This is bad...!
From the walls and floor of the mansion, a writhing presence crawled out, accompanied by a stench of decay. They were rotting, moving corpses—Ghouls.
I acted immediately. While I scanned for enemies and directed the escape route, Revy shot the approaching Ghouls in the head.
Revy
Hey, hey. They were quiet just a moment ago, and now they're suddenly in a welcoming mood?
Me
It seems the inhabitants sensed the intruder's presence and woke up.
Even so, the two of us managed to get close to the exit. But what appeared from the deepest part was a vampire with large fangs.
Revy
Tch... After Ghouls, now vampires? I knew a horror house wouldn't be a horror house without this.
Vampire
...Give it back...!
The vampire lunged at Revy, waving its ominous claws as if to reach for the jewel box she held.
Revy
So it's something precious? Sorry, but I'm taking it!
Revy immediately pulled the trigger, firing a burst aimed at its chest and head. The steel bullets pierced the vampire's body.
But even as the flesh tore and bones shattered, the vampire's body kept repairing itself.
Vampire
...Give it... back... my... heart...
Revy
Shut up! Just die already!
Revy kept firing bullets in rapid succession, not giving it a moment to heal.
Eventually, black miasma spewed from the wounds, drifting through the air like fog, and the body dissolved into the atmosphere.
Having cleared the obstacle, we burst out of the mansion. But just as we thought we had escaped...
I definitely felt a cold mist creeping up, brushing against my skin, mixed with the night wind.
Me
(No way... it's following us!?)
The scene shifts back to the present, to an alley behind the bustling street.
I ran, following Revy. I could feel the presence of the mist and the growling of Ghouls behind me.
Me
Revy, your ammo is...?
Revy
I know... Damn it, nothing goes right tonight.
She pulled a magazine from her jacket's inner pocket and loaded it. A dry click echoed.
Me
...What's inside that box...
Revy
Some nasty monster is desperate to get it back. It can't be anything good.
Revy
Let's see. I'll open it up. It might just be a jack-in-the-box.
Revy casually pried open the small box. Inside, a heart pulsed with an eerie thump-thump. It was alive. Undeniably, it was moving.
It was the core that supported the undead nature of the vampire that had been chasing us relentlessly. That was why it had come after us. No matter how far.
Me
...So, it really is that vampire's... heart.
Revy
Yeah, no mistake. You're making me laugh. A half-dead thing clinging to life.
For the residents of Loano Plra, where the "walking dead" gather, the Walking Dead might just be a source of ridicule.
Revy
Exorcism is the job of those damn nuns. If only we had at least some silver bullets...
Me
We need a plan. Something to break through this situation.
Revy
Hey, Ninja Boy. Do you have any secret strategy, like Zhuge Liang?
I didn't really have anything that could be called a strategy, just reckless ideas...
Me
I have a prototype grenade from the science team. But... the power is extremely high. It'll probably blow this whole area away.
I stopped walking and looked around at the surrounding buildings. Abandoned buildings, closed shops. If a massive explosion happened, it would quickly turn into a pile of rubble...
Revy looked surprised for a split second, but then she grinned.
Revy
Hah, is that for a kamikaze? Well, I don't mind crazy toys like that.
I clearly understood that this was a self-destructive act. The risk was too high.
Revy
Then I'll give you that firecracker as a present. It feels bad just taking and taking.
Me
But it's too dangerous...!
Revy
Listen. In situations like this, the one who gets scared loses.
Revy forcibly snatched the grenade from my hand and showed me a glinting, wicked smile.
Revy
The slowpokes are probably buried under the rubble. But you're different, aren't you, Ninja Boy?
Revy
Let's dance, Amigo!!
The explosion tore through the night.
A flash of light and a deafening roar. The mist and the Ghouls were blown away, and buildings collapsed. The silence of the night was destroyed in an instant.
We ran, weaving through the gaps in the rubble. The lingering echo of the explosion still rang in my eardrums.
There were still burning remains all around us, and smoke obscured our vision. The groans of the Undead were turning into something closer to their death throes.
Having escaped the hellish scene, we collapsed onto a convenient piece of rubble.
As I tried to steady my ragged breathing, I realized my hands were trembling.
Me
...We're alive, aren't we?
Revy
Yeah. I just have good luck in situations like this.
Revy answered with a wry smile, then let out a sigh. Her hair was disheveled with soot, but she looked somewhat satisfied.
Me
...That decision you made earlier. I wouldn't have been able to make it.
Revy
You overthink things, you know. You should try living more... in the moment.
I nodded silently, and Revy let out a breath before pulling out a cigarette.
The night was finally beginning to fade. The sky shifted from purple to a pale orange, and the eastern horizon started to lighten.
Me
At this time of day, the vampires can't come out, right? They should be weak to sunlight.
Revy
Burial successful. I could probably switch careers to being a gravedigger.
Revy lit the cigarette and slowly exhaled the smoke. It dissolved into the morning air.
Me
Revy... aren't you scared? Of that kind of life-or-death situation.
Revy
If I had time to be scared, I'd be reloading and running. That's how I've made it this far.
Revy
Besides, if you get scared, you won't survive in New Orleans.
Suddenly, Revy noticed my gaze and raised the corner of her mouth.
Revy
What? You want a smoke?
The offered cigarette. Normally I would refuse, but at the end of this night, I found myself wanting one.
I took just one and lit it. But I was unaccustomed to the purple smoke and immediately coughed.
Me
Cough, cough... I guess I can't pull off the cool act after all...
Revy
Haha, looks like you're still a baby, huh.
At the sound of her laughter, I couldn't help but smile faintly myself. For the first time, I could feel the darkness lifting.
Revy
Well, let's get this delivered and collect the reward. Ninja Boy, you did a fine job today.
I nodded silently and glanced at the dawn breaking behind me. The city had completely changed its face.
